content: claim-filing-core is SHARED between the ops branch and jobnimbus-bridge. Any core change on either side must be flagged in AGENT_HANDOFF.md and back-ported so the copies stay identical — no silent drift. Re-synced 2026-07-15 (adopted bridge improvements: carrier directory, callback confirmation, IVR phone lookup).

Peer-review loop with Codex works: he reproduces bugs before reporting; treat his findings as verified defects. Memory hardening round confirmed three real bugs (authority filtering, storage-root override losing seeds, PII guard bypass) that selftests now lock in.
Historical baseline: of 884 resolved files in the book, 47% closed and 53% were lost. Every recovered point of the lost rate is the value target.
Travelers is a slow-mover: active files sit a median 86.5 days in status vs 39 book-wide (n=10 files). Build extra follow-up cadence into every Travelers file.
Allstate historical close rate: 80% of 59 resolved files closed (n=156 total). Use as the baseline when judging whether a Allstate file is on track.
State Farm historical close rate: 81% of 27 resolved files closed (n=88 total). Use as the baseline when judging whether a State Farm file is on track.
Farmers historical close rate: 80% of 20 resolved files closed (n=63 total). Use as the baseline when judging whether a Farmers file is on track.

Adjuster fields are chronically empty (~27% filled across major carriers). Capturing the adjuster at first contact is a standing gap — every carrier email/call that names one should be written to the file immediately.
Aging reality: 48% of active files (159/329) sit untouched >= 14 days against the 2-week audit standard. Staleness is systemic, not an exception — triage should assume it.

Working-pipeline bottleneck: Photo File / Estimate Needed holds files a median 25 days (178 transitions) — the slowest high-volume WORKING stage. Estimate production is the muscle to speed up; files entering it need proactive photo/estimate pushes.

Closeout discipline gap: Review for Close holds files a median 36.3 days (43 transitions) — closeouts drift instead of resolving. Files entering closeout need a decision (archive or re-push), not a parking spot.

ESX files are encrypted by Xactimate (inner XACTDOC.ZIPXML is not readable XML) — never attempt to parse them for scope data. Use the Final Draft PDF render of our estimate instead; it parses cleanly (validated 110 line items + RCV against a manually-read estimate).

evidence.note: scope-miner build 2026-07-15, binary inspection of two ESX files

content: Initial carrier scopes are systematically a fraction of ours: across every parseable estimate pair (Farmers x2, USAA, Allstate, State Farm, Liberty Mutual), the carrier initial position ranged from net-$0/below-deductible to ~42% of our RCV. Gaps of $34k-$59k on the three fully-compared pairs. Treat every initial carrier estimate as an opening position, never a valuation.

Carrier omission pattern (3 fully-compared pairs, n small): the biggest recurring gaps vs our scope are detach-and-reset items, paint/seal, interior water damage, fascia/soffit, vents/caps, gutters/downspouts, and windows/screens. When reviewing any carrier scope, check these categories first.

Sub-deductible tactic observed at Allstate and Liberty Mutual: initial scope written small enough to net $0 (e.g., 3 shingles + rain cap = RCV $244 on a 35.7-square roof vs $5,000 deductible; a Below Deductible Settlement Letter against our $66.9k estimate). A sub-deductible initial scope on real storm damage is a signal to escalate, not close.

Some carrier scope PDFs are scanned images with no text layer (2 of 8 attempted) — scope:mine parses 0 items on them. OCR (pdftoppm+tesseract port from the old bridge branch) is the fix; until then, flag zero-item parses for manual read.

Workflow rule candidate: export the Final Draft PDF of every estimate to JobNimbus alongside the ESX — ESX is encrypted and unparseable, so the PDF is what makes a file scope-comparable (and appraisal/negotiation ready).
